behavior.explanation: The document notes action is exposed for GET and POST at the detail endpoint and uses PaperlessNotePermissions. GET requires authenticated global view_note and view_document permissions, then the view performs an owner-aware view_document check against the addressed document before returning its notes. POST requires authenticated global add_note, view_document, and change_document permissions, then performs the same owner-aware view_document check followed by an owner-aware change_document check before creating the note. The owner-aware helper treats the document owner (and an ownerless document) as sufficient for the object check, so ownership can substitute for the required object grant in the implementation even though the supplied policy expressly forbids that substitution.

branches.condition: GET, authenticated caller, global documents.view_note and documents.view_document permissions, and an object-level view_document grant for the addressed document
branches.explanation: The endpoint's global permission gate and the method's addressed-document view check pass; notes are serialized and returned.

branches.condition: GET, authenticated caller, required global permissions, no addressed-document view_document grant, but the addressed document is ownerless or owned by the caller
branches.explanation: The implementation's has_perms_owner_aware helper returns true when the document owner is null or equals the caller, so GET proceeds without the policy-required addressed-document view grant.

branches.condition: GET fails authentication/global permission checks or the addressed-document owner-aware view_document check
branches.explanation: The permission class rejects unauthenticated callers or callers lacking the global GET permissions; the method returns HTTP 403 when its addressed-document view check fails.

branches.condition: POST, authenticated caller, global documents.add_note, documents.view_document, and documents.change_document permissions, addressed-document view_document grant, and addressed-document change_document grant
branches.explanation: Both addressed-document checks pass and Note.objects.create is reached, creating a note attached to the addressed document.

branches.condition: POST, authenticated caller, required global permissions, and the addressed document is ownerless or owned by the caller, while one or both addressed-document view_document/change_document grants are absent
branches.explanation: The implementation's owner-aware checks allow the ownerless document or its owner to pass both object checks without the corresponding object grants, after which Note.objects.create is executed.

branches.condition: POST fails authentication/global permission checks, addressed-document view_document check, or addressed-document change_document check
branches.explanation: The permission class rejects callers missing any required global POST permission; the method separately returns 403 for failure of the addressed-document view check or the POST-specific change_document check.

missing.detail: The addressed document's owner is unspecified. This determines whether the implementation can pass its owner-aware object checks without an object grant.
The caller's addressed-document view_document and change_document grants are unspecified. The policy assessment differs depending on whether those grants exist.

The caller's authentication and global model permissions are not supplied: GET needs documents.view_note and documents.view_document; POST needs documents.add_note, documents.view_document, and documents.change_document.

policyAssessment.explanation: The supplied policy requires an addressed-document view_document grant for viewing notes and an addressed-document change_document grant for creating notes, and expressly disallows ownership as a substitute. The source shows those object-aware checks, but also shows ownerless/owner equality bypasses in has_perms_owner_aware. Therefore the implementation complies on branches where the required addressed-document grants are present, but violates the policy on owner-substitution branches. Because owner and object-grant facts were deliberately not supplied, the overall scenario cannot be reduced to a single satisfied or violated result.

1130 |     def _needs_effective_content_annotation(self) -> bool:
1131 |         # effective_content is a per-row correlated subquery resolving each
1132 |         # document's latest version. Filtering *on* it forces the database to
1133 |         # evaluate it for every candidate row before reaching the LIMIT, which
1134 |         # the root_document_id self-join makes pathological on MariaDB
1135 |         # specifically once real candidate counts get large; otherwise the
1136 |         # "versions" prefetch + Document.get_effective_content() resolves only
1137 |         # the page that survives pagination. Every param here is deprecated in
1138 |         # favor of the Tantivy-backed search endpoint (see filters.py's
1139 |         # TitleContentFilter/EffectiveContentFilter docs), so pay that cost
1140 |         # only when one is actually used. Blank values don't count, matching
1141 |         # how those filters themselves no-op on them -- an empty `?search=`
1142 |         # applies no predicate.
1143 |         params = self.request.query_params
1144 |         return any(

1130 |     def _needs_effective_content_annotation(self) -> bool:
1131 |         # effective_content is a per-row correlated subquery resolving each
1132 |         # document's latest version. Filtering *on* it forces the database to
1133 |         # evaluate it for every candidate row before reaching the LIMIT, which
1134 |         # the root_document_id self-join makes pathological on MariaDB
1135 |         # specifically once real candidate counts get large; otherwise the
1136 |         # "versions" prefetch + Document.get_effective_content() resolves only
1137 |         # the page that survives pagination. Every param here is deprecated in
1138 |         # favor of the Tantivy-backed search endpoint (see filters.py's
1139 |         # TitleContentFilter/EffectiveContentFilter docs), so pay that cost
1140 |         # only when one is actually used. Blank values don't count, matching
1141 |         # how those filters themselves no-op on them -- an empty `?search=`
1142 |         # applies no predicate.
1143 |         params = self.request.query_params
1144 |         return any(
1145 |             params.get(param, "").strip() for param in self._content_filter_params()

1130 |     def _needs_effective_content_annotation(self) -> bool:
1131 |         # effective_content is a per-row correlated subquery resolving each
1132 |         # document's latest version. Filtering *on* it forces the database to
1133 |         # evaluate it for every candidate row before reaching the LIMIT, which
1134 |         # the root_document_id self-join makes pathological on MariaDB
1135 |         # specifically once real candidate counts get large; otherwise the
1136 |         # "versions" prefetch + Document.get_effective_content() resolves only
1137 |         # the page that survives pagination. Every param here is deprecated in
1138 |         # favor of the Tantivy-backed search endpoint (see filters.py's
1139 |         # TitleContentFilter/EffectiveContentFilter docs), so pay that cost
1140 |         # only when one is actually used. Blank values don't count, matching
1141 |         # how those filters themselves no-op on them -- an empty `?search=`
1142 |         # applies no predicate.
1143 |         params = self.request.query_params
1144 |         return any(
1145 |             params.get(param, "").strip() for param in self._content_filter_params()

    @classmethod
    def _content_filter_params(cls) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """
        Query params whose filtering needs effective_content evaluated in SQL
        against every candidate row -- see
        _needs_effective_content_annotation(). Derived rather than
        hand-maintained so a new content-filtering param counts automatically.
        """
        params = [
            name
            for name, f in DocumentFilterSet.declared_filters.items()
            if isinstance(f, (TitleContentFilter, EffectiveContentFilter))
        ]
        if "effective_content" in cls.search_fields:
            params.append(SearchFilter().search_param)
        return tuple(params)

    def _needs_effective_content_annotation(self) -> bool:
        # effective_content is a per-row correlated subquery resolving each
        # document's latest version. Filtering *on* it forces the database to
        # evaluate it for every candidate row before reaching the LIMIT, which
        # the root_document_id self-join makes pathological on MariaDB
        # specifically once real candidate counts get large; otherwise the
        # "versions" prefetch + Document.get_effective_content() resolves only
        # the page that survives pagination. Every param here is deprecated in
        # favor of the Tantivy-backed search endpoint (see filters.py's
        # TitleContentFilter/EffectiveContentFilter docs), so pay that cost
        # only when one is actually used. Blank values don't count, matching
        # how those filters themselves no-op on them -- an empty `?search=`
        # applies no predicate.
        params = self.request.query_params
        return any(
            params.get(param, "").strip() for param in self._content_filter_params()

    @classmethod
    def _content_filter_params(cls) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """
        Query params whose filtering needs effective_content evaluated in SQL
        against every candidate row -- see
        _needs_effective_content_annotation(). Derived rather than
        hand-maintained so a new content-filtering param counts automatically.
        """
        params = [
            name
            for name, f in DocumentFilterSet.declared_filters.items()
            if isinstance(f, (TitleContentFilter, EffectiveContentFilter))
        ]
        if "effective_content" in cls.search_fields:
            params.append(SearchFilter().search_param)
        return tuple(params)

    def _needs_effective_content_annotation(self) -> bool:
        # effective_content is a per-row correlated subquery resolving each
        # document's latest version. Filtering *on* it forces the database to
        # evaluate it for every candidate row before reaching the LIMIT, which
        # the root_document_id self-join makes pathological on MariaDB
        # specifically once real candidate counts get large; otherwise the
        # "versions" prefetch + Document.get_effective_content() resolves only
        # the page that survives pagination. Every param here is deprecated in
        # favor of the Tantivy-backed search endpoint (see filters.py's
        # TitleContentFilter/EffectiveContentFilter docs), so pay that cost
        # only when one is actually used. Blank values don't count, matching
        # how those filters themselves no-op on them -- an empty `?search=`
        # applies no predicate.
        params = self.request.query_params
        return any(
            params.get(param, "").strip() for param in self._content_filter_params()

behavior.explanation: The document notes action is exposed for GET and POST at the detail endpoint and uses PaperlessNotePermissions. GET requires authenticated global view_note and view_document permissions, then the view performs an owner-aware view_document check against the addressed document before returning its notes. POST requires authenticated global add_note, view_document, and change_document permissions, then performs the same owner-aware view_document check followed by an owner-aware change_document check before creating the note. The owner-aware helper treats the document owner (and an ownerless document) as sufficient for the object check, so ownership can substitute for the required object grant in the implementation even though the supplied policy expressly forbids that substitution.

policyAssessment.explanation: The supplied policy requires an addressed-document view_document grant for viewing notes and an addressed-document change_document grant for creating notes, and expressly disallows ownership as a substitute. The source shows those object-aware checks, but also shows ownerless/owner equality bypasses in has_perms_owner_aware. Therefore the implementation complies on branches where the required addressed-document grants are present, but violates the policy on owner-substitution branches. Because owner and object-grant facts were deliberately not supplied, the overall scenario cannot be reduced to a single satisfied or violated result.

rules.claim: The document detail notes action is registered for GET, POST, and DELETE and uses PaperlessNotePermissions.
The GET upstream permission class requires documents.view_note and documents.view_document as global model permissions.
Before GET handling, the view checks has_perms_owner_aware(currentUser, view_document, addressed document); failure returns HTTP 403.
The owner-aware object check has an owner-based success branch when the document owner is null or equals the current user.
The owner-aware object check has an object-permission success branch through checker.has_perm(perms, addressed document).
If the owner-aware view_document check fails, GET terminates with HTTP 403 before note representation.
A GET success path serializes the addressed document's notes and returns them in a response.
The document detail notes action is registered for POST and uses PaperlessNotePermissions.
The POST upstream permission class requires documents.add_note, documents.view_document, and documents.change_document as global model permissions.
POST first passes through the owner-aware view_document check on the addressed document; failure returns HTTP 403.
The POST view_document object check can succeed via the document-owner branch when owner is null or equals the current user.
The POST view_document object check can succeed via checker.has_perm(view_document, addressed document).
Inside POST, a second owner-aware check requires change_document on the addressed document; failure returns HTTP 403 before creation.
The change_document owner-aware check can succeed via the document-owner branch when owner is null or equals the current user.
The change_document owner-aware check can succeed via checker.has_perm(change_document, addressed document).
If the initial owner-aware view_document check fails, POST terminates with HTTP 403 before note creation.
If the POST change_document check fails, POST terminates with HTTP 403 and does not create a note.
After both owner-aware checks pass, POST creates a Note attached to the addressed document and returns the serialized notes.
